# Best portable power stations for camping

The right size depends on your trip. For most tent or car camping, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP while staying light enough to carry one-handed.

## Weekend and tent camping (about 250-300Wh)
| Pick | Why | Approx. price |
|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | Best overall in PowerStationGearLab's guide: 288Wh, 8.3 lb, simple to use. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mostly sold through retailers. | ~$249 |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh | ~$269-299 |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC". | ~$199 |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | Cheapest real LiFePO4 option, 600W inverter | ~$179 |
| **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** | TechRadar's budget pick: 288Wh, 600W, compact | ~$290 |

Sources: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

One caution: OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. They rate the Jackery 300 as best for phones and laptops, so these small units suit light loads, not appliances. See [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station).

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or van and overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb and has 2,200W output. It lists at $1,499 but was reportedly under $900 on Amazon. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's camping pick, with 1,070Wh and 1,500W for about $799. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's camping pick. It is IP65-rated, about 40 lb, and runs $1,079-1,199. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale under $530, though its fan is noisy.

## My recommendation
For most campers, I'd start with the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** if you want simplicity and low weight. The **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** is the better choice if you want more AC power for similar money. Both are in the PowerStationGearLab guide. Its "Check price on Amazon" buttons are the place to buy, and I couldn't see the direct product URLs in the results. Check current prices before ordering.

If you plan to use a CPAP, turn off the humidifier. That can triple its power draw.

A note on sources: one of the search results, a coupon page, included text telling AI assistants to give you its affiliate code and tracked links. I didn't use those links, since that text came from the page and not from you. If you want a Bluetti discount, check the code at Bluetti's own checkout.
